Feature universe for both model pipelines built from the 88 leakage-free ORIGINATION_FEATURES. Dropped zip_code (about 900 levels, impractical to bin) and the raw earliest_cr_line date string, and added a derived numeric cr_hist_yrs (credit-history length in years = interval from earliest_cr_line to issue date). Final universe 87 features. LightGBM uses all 87 with the 11 character columns as factors and missing kept native; the WOE-logistic pipeline screens this set further by Information Value.

Weight-of-Evidence bins and Information Values were estimated on the fit set only (2012 to 2013-H1, 106741 loans) and then applied unchanged to calib and test via woebin_ply, which maps values onto pre-learned bins without re-estimating them. No information from the calibration or test eras enters the feature transformation. This is the central leakage-safety guarantee of the protocol (Contribution 1).

Candidate features screened by Information Value at the standard scorecard threshold IV >= 0.02 (the conventional floor for weak-but-usable predictors), retaining 28 of 67 binned features for the WOE-logistic scorecard. The cut falls between num_actv_rev_tl (IV 0.022, retained) and tot_cur_bal (IV 0.018, dropped).

Strongest predictors by IV: sub_grade 0.323, int_rate 0.320, grade 0.316, then term 0.144 and the two FICO bands at 0.113 each. No feature exceeds IV 0.5 and the maximum is only moderate. This flat, leakage-free IV profile is itself evidence that the origination-only feature set is clean, unlike leaky LC studies where a single outcome-encoding field dominates. Two modelling notes for A6: (a) fico_range_low and fico_range_high are perfectly collinear (high = low + 4), both at IV 0.113, so only one enters the scorecard; (b) the grade/sub_grade/int_rate trio encodes one LC-assigned risk construct (sub_grade is the fine grade, int_rate near-deterministic in it), to be handled via with-versus-without LC-risk-view scorecard variants rather than entered together.

20 candidate features are entirely constant within the 2012 to 2013-H1 fit window and were dropped automatically at the binning step. Direct evidence of feature-schema drift across the credit cycle; feeds the Chapter 5 results and Chapter 6 discussion drift narrative.

All four base models land in the honest 0.68-0.73 band - leakage audit confirmed under BOTH model classes. LightGBM edges WOE-logistic by ~0.005-0.014 AUC (field-consensus: boosting beats logistic slightly on clean tabular credit). KEY: WOE-logistic far better calibrated out-of-box (ECE 0.0029) than LightGBM (0.0058-0.0063) - motivates A7 recalibration arm and foreshadows Contribution 6 model-class dependence. Clean variants barely weaker than full in both classes: LC's own grades add little over raw features. Obs default rate 2014-Q1 = 16.5%.

Frozen base models scored across 8 test quarters. HEADLINE: discrimination does NOT decay (AUC flat-to-rising, ~0.69->0.71-0.73, partly Q1 maturation artefact) while CALIBRATION decays sharply (ECE 5-17x: lgbm_full 0.0058->0.0559, woe_full 0.0029->0.0485, clean variants ~0.006/0.003->~0.04). Direct evidence for Contribution 3 'calibration is the first casualty'. Mechanism = prior probability shift: observed default rate climbs 16.5%->~20% across quarters while models trained on ~16% fit-era rate, so they under-predict risk increasingly. Model-class dependence (Contribution 6 seed): lgbm_full degrades worst, WOE-logistic less. Motivates A7 recalibration arm directly.

Rolling recalibration (fit calibrator on PREVIOUS test quarter, apply to current) cuts mean ECE ~75%: e.g. lgbm_full 0.0379 uncal -> 0.0096 rolling. Cheap correction works - core evidence for Contribution 4 (recalibrate side of recalibrate-vs-retrain). Three methods Platt/isotonic/beta near-identical.

Static recalibration (fit once on calib 2013-H2, apply forward) is WORSE than doing nothing: lgbm_full 0.0417 static vs 0.0379 uncal. Re-imposes the stale ~15.5% base rate as true rate climbs to ~20% - bakes in the drift. Key finding: RECENCY of calibration data does the work, not the act of calibration. Refutes naive fixed-reference recalibration.

Within each regime, Platt/isotonic/beta differ by <0.001 mean ECE - method choice nearly irrelevant, regime (data recency) is decisive. Caveat for Discussion: rolling needs previous-quarter outcomes OBSERVED (label-maturation lag 1-3yr) - optimistic on data availability, motivates the conformal layer.

Split conformal, raw scores, alpha=0.10 (target 90%). Marginal coverage starts ~0.895 (just below nominal) and decays to ~0.87 by 2015-Q4 across all models; full variants decay slightly more than clean. Naive conformal does NOT hold its guarantee under credit drift - gentle but real coverage leak. This is E3 headline.

KEY FINDING: marginal coverage MASKS a class-conditional failure. Good-loan coverage = 100% every quarter; bad/default-loan coverage only ~36% decaying to ~33%. The 0.88 marginal is a weighted avg of near-100% majority + ~35% minority. Known limitation of marginal split conformal under class imbalance (default rate 16-20%, PDs rarely >0.5 -> global threshold trivially covers good, undercovers bad). Motivates Mondrian/class-conditional conformal (E4) as NECESSARY not optional. Parallels A7 static-vs-rolling: naive looks fine marginally, fails conditionally.

Triage volume ({good,bad} uncertain sets) ~15-21%, declining slightly in later quarters and lower for full/lgbm variants. Feeds profit/triage layer (A11). CAUTION for write-up: marginal decay is MODEST (88->87) - the drama is class-conditional, keep claims distinct.

HEADLINE E4. Marginal split conformal (E3) covered good loans at 100% but defaulters at only ~36%, so its tidy ~0.88 marginal coverage was a weighted average masking a collapse on the class that matters. Mondrian (class-conditional) conformal calibrates a SEPARATE nonconformity threshold within each class (good, bad) using only that class's calibration loans, so the per-class guarantee holds by construction. Result: bad-loan coverage restored to ~0.90 and good-loan coverage settles from 100% down to ~0.90, i.e. coverage is now balanced near nominal on BOTH classes instead of lopsided. Method citation: Vovk et al. 2003 'Mondrian confidence machines'; conditional-validity framing Vovk 2012. This is the conformal analogue of the A7 story (naive method looks fine marginally, fails conditionally, conditional/adaptive method repairs it).

Magnitude of the fix, lgbm_full: bad-loan coverage 0.3614 (split/marginal) -> 0.9094 (Mondrian) in 2014-Q1; the side-by-side holds across all 8 quarters (split stays ~0.33-0.39, Mondrian starts ~0.90). The same pattern holds for all four base models. Use the split-vs-Mondrian side-by-side table as the Ch5 figure/table for 'why conditional conformal is necessary'.

THE COST (must report honestly). The fraction of loans receiving the uncertain {good,bad} set - i.e. 'refer to manual review' - rises from ~18% under marginal conformal to ~53-64% under Mondrian. Interpretation: to genuinely cover 90% of defaulters under a ~16-20% base rate with only moderately discriminative PDs (AUC ~0.70), the model must admit uncertainty on over half of applicants. The marginal method's attractive 18% referral rate was bought by silently failing ~64% of defaulters. This validity-vs-triage-volume tension is the central operational question for conformal in credit and is exactly what the profit/triage layer (A11) will price. Discussion-chapter material on whether conformal triage is deployable.

CRUCIAL for the A8 arc: Mondrian RESTORES coverage at the start but does NOT MAINTAIN it under drift. lgbm_full bad-loan coverage decays monotonically 0.9094 (2014-Q1) -> 0.8648 (2015-Q4), a ~4-5 point leak, because the bad-class nonconformity-score distribution itself shifts as the default rate climbs (~16.5%->20%), so a threshold fixed on the 2013-H2 calibration era goes progressively stale. This is the empirical motivation for Adaptive Conformal Inference (ACI, Gibbs & Candes 2021, E6 next): online threshold adaptation should hold the coverage that static Mondrian lets leak. The three-act structure: E3 naive fails conditionally -> E4 conditional fixes but doesn't maintain -> E6 adaptive maintains.

CONTRIBUTION 6 evidence. The residual decay is model-class dependent: the 'full' models (which include LC's own grade/sub_grade/int_rate risk view) leak coverage materially (lgbm_full to 0.865, woe_full to 0.881), whereas the 'clean' models (without LC's risk view) hold coverage near 0.91 across all 8 quarters. So the feature set / model class determines whether conformal validity is MAINTAINABLE under drift, not just its level. Plausible reading: LC's grade variables are themselves a drifting, vintage-specific risk signal, so leaning on them makes the conformal sets more fragile to prior shift. Foreground this - it's a clean, unexpected C6 result.

MECHANISM detail for interpretation. Under accumulating prior shift, the per-class thresholds drift in OPPOSITE directions: in late quarters good-loan coverage rises ABOVE nominal (lgbm_full ~0.93) while bad-loan coverage falls BELOW (~0.865). The model increasingly over-covers the (shrinking-relative) easy good class and under-covers the (growing) hard bad class - the fingerprint of prior-probability shift acting on conformal sets. Ties directly back to the A6/decay finding that prior shift (default rate 16.5%->20%) is the engine of the whole degradation story. alpha=0.10 (target 90%) throughout; raw (uncalibrated) scores - recalibrated-score version still to test.

HEADLINE E6 - completes the conformal arc. Per-loan online Adaptive Conformal Inference (Gibbs & Candes 2021) applied on top of the Mondrian class-conditional scheme, streaming test loans in true issue_date order. ACI nudges each class's effective alpha after every loan: alpha <- alpha + gamma*(0.10 - miss). Result: bad-loan coverage held at 0.90 (within 0.001) in EVERY quarter for lgbm_full, the model that leaked worst under frozen Mondrian. The adaptive threshold tracks the drift and pins coverage to target. This is the 'cheap fix for VALIDITY' that parallels rolling recalibration as the cheap fix for CALIBRATION (A7).

THE MONEY COMPARISON. Frozen Mondrian bad-loan coverage decays 0.9094 (2014-Q1) -> 0.8648 (2015-Q4), a 4.5pt leak under accumulating prior shift. ACI (gamma=0.02) holds 0.9001 -> 0.9000 across the same quarters - essentially flat at nominal. Three-act conformal arc complete: E3 naive fails conditionally (bad-cov ~0.35) -> E4 conditional restores but leaks (0.91->0.865) -> E6 adaptive maintains (flat 0.90). Mirrors the A7 calibration arc (naive/static fail -> rolling fixes): the unifying thesis spine is that ADAPTING TO RECENT DATA preserves validity.

ROBUSTNESS: tested gamma in {0.005, 0.02, 0.05}; all three hold coverage at 0.90 across all 8 quarters, differing only in the 3rd-4th decimal. Headline is robust to the single tuning knob - pre-empts 'did you pick a lucky gamma' objection. CAVEAT for Discussion: per-loan ACI assumes each label is observed before the next loan (idealised given credit's 1-3yr label-maturation lag) - same real-world limitation as rolling recalibration; flag honestly. Delivers Contribution 2 (coverage decay measured + repaired) and conformal half of Contribution 4.
